subject.title: fix(telegram): surface diagnostic warning when inline keyboard buttons silently dropped due to 64-byte callback_data limit

question: Is an operator log sufficient when Telegram keyboard controls are removed, or must the message-tool caller receive a structured partial-delivery warning or failure?
rationale: The linked report concerns safety-gated workflows where ok:true can be interpreted as successful control delivery; code inspection cannot decide the intended caller contract.

options.title: Expose Partial Delivery
options.body: Return a structured caller-visible diagnostic while preserving successful text delivery, so agents can react when controls were omitted.

options.title: Keep Operator Warning
options.body: Retain ok:true and treat a reason-specific gateway warning as the supported observability contract.

options.title: Fail The Send
options.body: Reject the whole message when any requested Telegram control exceeds the transport limit.

recommendation.title: Expose Partial Delivery
recommendation.body: Return a structured caller-visible diagnostic while preserving successful text delivery, so agents can react when controls were omitted.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history shows repeated ownership of Telegram interactive resolution and callback shaping.
